about: A small fixed dataset for checking the deterministic detectors and for comparing prompts or models. Labels are human judgments written before any detector was run. Do not edit to make a score pass.

sources.text: We rewrote our onboarding flow three times in 2025. The first rewrite added a product tour and activation did not move. The second removed the tour and cut signup from six fields to two, and activation rose from 31 percent to 38 percent. The third removed the invite-teammates step that nobody finished, and activation reached 47 percent in two weeks. Support tickets about setup fell by a third.

post.hook: Activation went from 31 to 47 percent after we deleted one step.
post.body: We rewrote onboarding three times. The tour changed nothing. Cutting signup to two fields lifted activation to 38 percent. Removing the invite-teammates step that nobody finished took it to 47 percent in two weeks.
post.cta: Which step would you delete from your product?

post.hook: Churn is decided in the first week.
post.body: Customers who never reach a first result rarely come back. Show the first result early and everything downstream gets easier. We saw churn on annual plans fall to 4 percent once people committed.
Always believe in yourself and keep working hard. Great things happen to people who never give up. Stay focused and the results will follow.

post.hook: Our best pricing change took ten minutes.
post.body: We moved the plan toggle above the fold. Nothing else. People finally saw that annual plans existed, and more of them picked one. We had spent weeks debating discounts when the real problem was visibility.
post.cta: What have you hidden from your own customers?
